A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCBM research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching v2 Appendix E to v3 Appendix F.

before.justification: v2 reports original leakage, accuracy, interpretability, and intervention experiments on four benchmarks in Section 4, plus the spiral classification experiment in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds AwA2 results, additional comparisons and metrics, correlation analysis, and random-concept intervention results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The objectives and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. However, v3 Appendix F.1 newly describes an MLP representation head, whereas retained Section 2.4 and Algorithm 1 specify fixed concept-to-prototype mappings. These conflicting descriptions prevent determining whether the implementation changed or only its documentation. The auxiliary nuisance latent in Section 6 is future work.

E1.justification: v3 adds AwA2 animal-class classification, using 20 attributes as concepts and the remaining 65 as task-related nuisances. The four existing benchmarks and the spiral experiment are retained. This extends coverage within the existing image-classification setting.

E2.justification: Energy-based CBMs, or ECBMs, are newly evaluated in the leakage and accuracy comparisons in Tables 3–6 and the representation comparisons in Figure 4. Other comparator families are retained. ECBM does not participate in the intervention plots.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with OIS alongside CKA and disentanglement, and random concept selection alongside lowest-confidence interventions. It also specifies AwA2 training and preprocessing settings. The reported CUB nuisance partition changes from 20 to 15 groups, correcting the inconsistency with 27 total groups; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E and Figure 10 test whether intervention findings depend on selecting low-confidence concepts by evaluating random selection on CIFAR-10, CUB, and AwA2. New Table 7 examines whether interpretability metrics track nuisance leakage. These add substantive policy-robustness and metric-validation analyses beyond the retained gamma comparisons.

E5.justification: Existing ± table reporting is retained. v3 adds uncertainty shading to Figure 5 and new Figure 10, p-values for rank correlations in Table 7, and discussion of variation across seeds in Appendix E. Run counts and the meaning of the shaded bands remain unspecified; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 retain existing entries but add ECBM and AwA2 results. Figure 4 adds OIS scores and expanded comparisons; Table 7 and Figure 10 supply new correlation and intervention results. Two existing CKA values also change: ARCBM on Shapes3D from 57.58 to 57.78, and SCBM on MPI3D from 86.83 to 86.93.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the joint-distribution factorization by adding the missing p(c,n) factor to p(x|c,n)p(y|x). The principal variational objectives, Appendix B derivations, and Appendix D mathematical treatment are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain unchanged. Section 3 adds an explicit priority claim: this is the first work to use information theory both to identify the underlying CBM design flaw and to address it through a per-latent variational information bottleneck.

C2.justification: v3 proposes CKA/OIS as practical gamma-selection proxies when nuisances are unobserved, qualifies gamma-insensitivity of interventions, and links similar AwA2 intervention performance to low leakage. Section 6 newly acknowledges incomplete nuisance removal on high-variance datasets and possible backbone-capacity dependence, materially qualifying applicability and the previously stronger elimination narrative.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds AwA2 preprocessing and training details, including ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 and 120 epochs, plus head-size and parameter-count disclosures. The new head descriptions conflict with retained specifications elsewhere. The same code URL moves from Section 4 to a dedicated Code Availability section; no changed resource availability is established.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for ECBM, OIS, AwA2, and Debole et al. (2025), while removing Xu et al. (2020) on usable information. Section 3 more explicitly distinguishes the proposed objective from prior leakage-measurement work and asserts priority. Most related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, and Sections 4.2–4.3. Section 6 expands to limitations and future directions, code availability receives its own section, and the experimental-details appendix moves from E to F. Most method exposition, proofs, and the overall narrative order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The conference template changes headers, typography, and reference layout. Central experimental displays are substantially expanded: Figure 4 grows from two heatmaps to three, Figure 5 gains an AwA2 panel and uncertainty shading, tables gain comparator rows and dataset columns, and Table 7 and Figure 10 are added.

improvement.justification: Random-selection interventions address v2's reliance on one intervention policy, while OIS and correlation analysis strengthen scrutiny of the interpretability evidence. Added limitations clarify incomplete nuisance removal. These provide a limited overall improvement, tempered by conflicting representation-head specifications and unspecified uncertainty-band definitions; the central method and proofs are essentially unchanged.
